ai.title: Remove binary smoke test from CLI update flow
ai.summary: Removed `runSmokeTest` from `cli/release/index.js` and `cli/release-staging/index.js`. This eliminates a Windows EPERM error caused by spawning the downloaded binary and reduces update latency. The update flow now moves the binary to its final location immediately after download.

eli5.text: When you update this command-line tool, it no longer runs a quick test on the newly downloaded program before using it. This test was causing the update to freeze or fail on Windows computers, and removing it makes the update finish faster. If you watch an update happen today, you'll see it skip the "Verifying download" step and go straight to putting the new version in place.

ai.title: Remove streamingAgents prop drilling in CLI blocks
ai.summary: Removes `streamingAgents` prop from CLI block components (`AgentBlockGrid`, `BlocksRenderer`, `ToolBranch`, etc.) and adds `memo` to `MessageBlock` and `MessageAttachments`. `ToolBranch` now derives `isStreaming` directly from `useChatStore` state instead of receiving it via props. This eliminates unnecessary re-renders caused by prop drilling and ensures components only update when their specific streaming state changes.

eli5.text: When you're watching an assistant work through a series of steps in the terminal, the screen used to repaint more often than necessary because the same 'is it still thinking?' status was passed down through many layers of display pieces. Now, that status is fetched from a single shared location and the display pieces that show your messages and files have also been taught to skip re-rendering unless something they care about actually changes, so the terminal output refreshes more smoothly while an assistant is working. It is live today for anyone using the terminal version of the assistant.

ai.title: CLI release bumped to 1.0.590
ai.summary: The CLI release package `cli/release/package.json` was bumped from 1.0.589 to 1.0.590 as part of the 2026-01-20/21 release sequence. This bump aggregates four user-facing improvements: the CLI agent mode rename from `test` to `work` (with `review` retained), default-collapsed `set_output` tool blocks, a new `cancelled` status for interrupted subagents, and the removal of the binary smoke test from the update flow. Internal refactors in `cli/release/index.js` and `cli/release-staging/index.js` now move the downloaded binary to its final location immediately after download.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version field bumped from 1.0.589 to 1.0.590 in the codebuff release package manifest (release-bump commit 1756f703).

eli5.text: Version 1.0.590 of the Freebuff command-line tool ships with cleaner agent workflows, a tidier display for automated steps, and faster, smoother updates. The built-in coding agents now use simpler "work" and "review" modes instead of the previous "test" mode, so you can more easily switch between building features and checking your work. Noisy intermediate output (like JSON from automated setup steps) is now collapsed by default, keeping your terminal readable, and when you cancel an agent mid-task it now clearly shows a "cancelled" status in red instead of hanging. The app-update process no longer runs a slow built-in test on Windows, which means updates download and install more quickly and avoid a past error. Finally, background display updates are now smarter about redrawing only the parts that actually changed, making everything feel a bit more responsive. Upgrading gives you a faster, less cluttered, and more reliable command-line experience.

ai.title: Exclude commander agents from pruned context
ai.summary: Added 'commander' and 'commander-lite' to the exclusion list in agents/context-pruner.ts. Prevents their output from being pruned during context management. Scope limited to the core agent context pruning logic. No migration or breaking changes required.

eli5.text: When the system runs low on space to keep track of everything, it usually deletes details about which helper it was talking to so it can keep the important parts. It now leaves alone the special helpers called 'commander' and 'commander-lite', so their full output stays in memory instead of being trimmed. You wouldn't notice this directly, but if you were using one of those helpers, its responses will be kept in full rather than summarized or cut off.

ai.title: Add programmatic handleSteps to CLI agents
ai.summary: Implements `handleSteps` generator functions in `.agents` CLI definitions to enforce programmatic tmux session management. Replaces LLM-driven shell commands with structured logic that parses `run_terminal_command` results, validates exit codes, and extracts session names directly from stdout. Updates `claude-code-cli.ts`, `codebuff-local-cli.ts`, `codex-cli.ts`, and `gemini-cli.ts` to serialize constants within the generator, ensuring robust session initialization independent of model adherence to prompt instructions.

eli5.text: When the system starts up one of its four built-in helpers (Claude, Codebuff, Codex, or Gemini), it now launches your terminal session on its own without needing the AI to be the one actually typing the command, so you don't have to worry about the session starting up reliably. It still starts a fresh terminal session at a specific size, and your work is still isolated from everything else, but the process is automated so you don't have to babysit the command being run correctly.

ai.title: Fix retry detection and narrow grant reads
ai.summary: Billing `getOrderedActiveGrants` now uses a UNION query to always include the last active grant even if its balance is zero, ensuring debt is correctly attributed to the lowest-priority grant. Transaction retry logic in `packages/internal/src/db/transaction.ts` now traverses nested error causes to extract valid PostgreSQL error codes, preventing false negatives for wrapped errors. Changes affect `packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts` and `packages/internal/src/db/transaction.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system figures out which of your prepaid credit grants should cover a charge, it now always includes your last active grant even if its balance is zero, so debt is correctly assigned to the lowest-priority grant instead of being skipped. Separately, the system's automatic retry logic for failed billing operations now looks through the full chain of nested error causes from the database to find valid retry codes, preventing false failures when errors are wrapped in additional layers. Both fixes are live today and affect how your account's credit consumption and billing retries are handled during active sessions.

ai.title: Refactor tmux session management with JSON output and robust parsing
ai.summary: Agent definitions in `claude-code-cli.ts`, `codebuff-local-cli.ts`, `codex-cli.ts`, and `gemini-cli.ts` now parse JSON output from `tmux-cli.sh` to extract session names and error states. The complex, nested parsing logic was replaced with a streamlined check for `stdout`, `stderr`, and `exitCode` within the JSON object. System prompts in `cli-agent-prompts.ts` were updated to reflect that session management is now handled automatically, removing instructions for manual `tmux-cli.sh start` command construction. `codebuff-local-cli.ts` also added `skipPrepPhase: true`.

eli5.text: When you start an AI coding agent, it now automatically launches a workspace session and tells you the session name in a message, so you no longer need to manually open one yourself. Behind the scenes, the agent reads a structured status report from the session tool to confirm whether the session started properly or ran into an error. If you looked, you'd see the agent skip any manual session-setup step and simply announce the ready-to-use session name for you to work in.

ai.title: fix(cli): resolve message queue race conditions and add recovery
ai.summary: CLI message queue refactored to prevent race conditions via synchronous state initialization and a 60-second watchdog timer. `use-message-queue.ts` separates user-pause state from system-busy state and adds `processNextMessage` logic. `use-send-message.ts` sets `isChainInProgressRef` synchronously before async work and introduces `resetEarlyReturnState` helper for error recovery. `send-message.ts` fixes history truncation assignment bug.

eli5.text: When you send multiple messages to the assistant in quick succession, the program now waits for each one to finish before starting the next, instead of accidentally mixing them up. Behind the scenes, the system starts each message-processing step immediately and synchronously, then adds a 60-second safety timer that resets things automatically if a step gets stuck. If an error happens early on, it cleanly clears out the stuck state so the next message can proceed without hesitation. You would notice that queued messages are processed in the correct order, and the assistant no longer freezes or skips responses when you type quickly.

ai.title: Token count API tracks model and input tokens
ai.summary: The agent runtime now passes the active model to the token count API. The web endpoint moved analytics tracking to post-success, logging the resolved Anthropic model ID and input token count. Model IDs are converted from OpenRouter format to Anthropic format before counting. Default fallback remains claude-opus-4-5-20251101.

eli5.text: When the assistant counts how many words you've sent in a conversation, it now also figures out which model (like Claude Opus or Claude Sonnet) is being used and includes the total input token count in its tracking. This means the analytics system gets more accurate information about what model is actually running and how much text it's processing, defaulting to Claude Opus 4.5 when the model isn't specified. The tracking also moved to after the token counting finishes successfully, so you only log successful counts rather than failed attempts. Who this affects: anyone using the token counting service will now have their actual model and input token totals recorded in analytics.

ai.title: Context pruner adds 1k token fudge factor
ai.summary: agents/context-pruner.ts introduces a 1000-token fudge factor to the context length check. Pruning now triggers when `contextTokenCount + 1000` exceeds `maxContextLength`, causing earlier summarization. This ensures a safety buffer before hard limits.

eli5.text: Your assistant will now start summarizing the conversation a little sooner when things are getting long. Behind the scenes, the system now keeps a roughly 1,000-word safety buffer before it decides a chat has gotten too large, so it condenses earlier instead of hitting a hard limit. If you chat for a while on a single topic, you may notice your previous messages getting summarized before the conversation becomes unwieldy.

ai.title: Fix context-pruner threshold tests for fudge factor
ai.summary: Test updates align context-pruner threshold assertions with 1000 token fudge factor logic. Cases verify no prune at `max - fudge` and prune at `max`. Covers `agents/__tests__/context-pruner.test.ts`.

eli5.text: Today, the assistant's memory manager got better at deciding when a conversation is getting too long. Previously, it would wait until you were exactly at the limit before summarizing, which was too late. Now it starts summarizing when you're 1,000 words away from the limit, giving it a small buffer. This means your longer conversations will be preserved more reliably before getting summarized.

ai.title: CI split billing integration tests into dedicated postgres job
ai.summary: CI workflow now runs `packages/billing` integration tests in a dedicated `test-billing-integration` job with a PostgreSQL 16 service container. The general `test-integration` job excludes `.agents` and `packages/billing` from its matrix, focusing on packages without database dependencies. `fail-fast: false` added to test strategies to allow independent package failures. Billing tests execute `db:migrate` via `packages/internal` before running `*.integration.test.ts` files.

eli5.text: The CI workflow now runs the billing package's integration tests in a new dedicated job that spins up a PostgreSQL 16 service container, while the general integration test job no longer includes that package or the agents package in its matrix. If you look at the GitHub Actions pipeline, you can see a separate test-billing-integration job with its own Postgres service, and the main test-integration job has been simplified to skip packages needing a database. Both jobs now use fail-fast: false so one package's failure doesn't cancel others. This change is live today and affects how integration tests run in CI.

eli5.text: When the billing system's automated tests run, they need to use a temporary test database instead of the real one. Previously, pulling in a shared helper function would accidentally connect to the production database before the test setup could redirect it. The test now carries its own copy of that helper, so tests start against the right database every time. Nothing about how your bill is calculated changed; only the test setup became more reliable.

ai.title: Set DATABASEURL at job level in CI billing tests
ai.summary: CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now defines `DATABASE_URL` at the `test-billing-integration` job level. This change ensures the environment variable explicitly overrides any secrets injection that might occur during the workflow run. The scope is limited to the GitHub Actions CI configuration for billing integration tests. The hardcoded URL `postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/testdb` matches the local Postgres service container.

eli5.text: Starting today, the billing tests that run automatically for the development team now always use the same local database address when checking the billing integration. Previously, an injected secret could interfere with the test settings; now the database URL is fixed at the job level so tests behave predictably. You won't see this change unless you're looking at the internal test setup, but it helps catch billing bugs before they affect live subscription handling.

ai.summary: CI workflow adds step setting `DATABASE_URL` to local test container after SDK build. Prevents injected secrets from overriding test DB config. Affects `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Uses `>> $GITHUB_ENV` for step-scoped env override.

eli5.text: When the company's automated testing system runs checks on new software, it briefly sets aside any secret login details it might normally use and points the check at a temporary, local test database instead. This stops the real secrets from accidentally overriding the test setup during the testing step. The fix is a small one-line addition to the testing workflow and is live today for anyone whose code passes through the automated check system.
